current_answer: Three different routes exist today: fal H3 Max Director is a hosted open WebRTC session, the inspected FastH3 route is buffered short-clip playout, and local MiniMax H3 is a short-clip workflow. None of the inspected sources establishes a cheap, proven self-hosted 24/7 route.

catalogue_card.question: Which AI video route can actually stay live?
catalogue_card.text: The headline hides three products: open sessions, buffered clips, and offline local renders. See the price, hardware, and failure condition before you build.

summary: fal's current H3 Max Director page describes an interactive WebRTC session, priced by generated second and limited public-session duration; its terms need a current check before purchase.
Reactor's FastH3 reference is a queued clip system. Its reported playback-rate profile uses four B200 GPUs and still needs a ready buffer.
Local MiniMax H3 can be a short-clip experiment, but community low-VRAM reports do not show live throughput or a general hardware recommendation.
uncertainty: fal documents conflicting Director session details across pages; the newer endpoint page is used provisionally.
No pool test, invoice, uptime log, or end-to-end latency measurement exists.
Project and community performance reports are condition-specific and not independently reproduced.
freshness_note: This first public map was checked on 10 September 2026. Pricing, session limits, model versions, and workflow compatibility can change quickly.
